name: Ahban
title: Descendant of Judah in the Jerahmeel line
summary: Ahban is known exclusively from the genealogy in 1 Chronicles, where he is listed as a son of Abishur and Abihail in the Jerahmeelite branch of the tribe of Judah. This lineage traces back through Jerahmeel, Hezron, and Perez to Judah himself. Along with his brother Molid, Ahban makes up the descendants of Abishur. No actions or stories are attached to him, but his presence in the genealogy reflects the thorough preservation of Judah's tribal history. The genealogies in Chronicles served, among other things, to document belonging and inheritance rights, especially in the period after the Babylonian exile.
roles: Member of the Jerahmeel line in the tribe of Judah

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
keyEvents.description: Ahban is mentioned as a son of Abishur and Abihail in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. Together with his brother Molid, he forms part of Abishur's descendants within the Jerahmeel branch, a side line that goes through Hezron and Perez.

versions.summary: Ahban is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles in the family tree of the tribe of Judah. He was the son of Abishur and his wife Abihail. He is known only from his place in the genealogy and has no recorded actions described in the Bible.

versions.reason: [minor] The title contains a typo: 'Etterkommmer' should be 'Etterkommer' (three m's instead of two).; [major] Ahban is mentioned only in a genealogy in 1 Chronicles 2 and belongs to the Jerahmeel line within the tribe of Judah. The genealogy extends back to the patriarchal period, and there is no information placing him specifically in the united monarchy. 'Patriarchs' is a more appropriate era since these are early lineage records from Judah, although uncertainty remains great.; [minor] The roles array is empty. Even for someone known only from a genealogy, it should include at least one role, such as 'Descendant of Judah' or 'Member of the Jerahmeel line'.; [minor] The fourth key event ('Placement in Judah's tribal history') refers to 1 Chron 2:1–5, which deals generally with Judah's sons and does not mention Ahban directly. This connection to Ahban is weak and may be misleading.; [minor] The title uses 'Jerakmeels' while the description uses 'Jerakmeels'. In the first key event, 'Jerakhmeel-linjen' is used with an 'h'. Spelling should be consistent – 'Jerakhmeel' is the most common Norwegian form.; [minor] The summary is acceptable but could include that Ahban specifically belongs to the Jerahmeel line, providing more context for his placement in the genealogy.

versions.reason: [minor] The summary is very similar to the previous version (version 1). It should be rephrased to provide a fresher and more distinct text.; [minor] The three key events overlap significantly – all concern the same verse (1 Chr 2:29) and the same genealogical context. It may be better to combine them into one or two more focused events to avoid repetition.; [minor] The time period 'patriarchs' can be discussed. Ahban belongs to the Jerahmeel line in the tribe of Judah, and his actual lifespan is unknown. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles cover many generations. Nevertheless, given that Perez and Hezron lived in the patriarchal era/early Egyptian sojourn, 'patriarchs' can be defended for a near descendant, but it remains uncertain.

He belongs to the Jerahmeel branch of the tribe of Judah—a side line that goes through Ram, Hezron, and Perez. versions.title: Descendant of Judah in the Jerahmeel line
versions.reason: [major] Ahban belongs to the Jerahmeel line in the tribe of Judah. This lineage extends far beyond the patriarchal period. Although his exact lifespan is unknown, the genealogy places him several generations after Judah, likely during the time of the judges or the united monarchy. 'patriarchs' is too early.; [minor] Verses 25-27 concern Jerahmeel and his sons, while Ahban is specifically mentioned in verse 29 (the sons of Abishur). Verse 28 mentions Onam. It is most precise to focus on verse 29 as the central reference, possibly with verse 28 for context regarding Abishur's place.

footnotes.text: The name Ahban (Hebrew: אַחְבָּן) may be composed of 'ach' (brother) and a root form that possibly means 'wise' or 'prudent'. The name occurs only in 1 Chron. 2:29 and is thus a hapax legomenon (a word/name that appears only once) in the biblical text.

The Jerahmeel line forms a side branch of the tribe of Judah that does not belong to the messianic lineage through David. The extensive genealogies in Chronicles likely served an important practical function after the Babylonian exile, including documenting family and property rights upon return to the land.

Abihail (Hebrew: אֲבִיחַיִל) means 'my father is strength/power'. The name is used for several different people in the Old Testament, both men and women, showing that it was a common Semitic name in biblical times.

The genealogies in Chronicles chapters 1–9 serve as a theological framework linking Israel's history back to creation. Even individuals like Ahban, who have no narrative attached to them, confirm the completeness of God's people's family trees and the careful preservation of lineages in Israelite tradition.

Jerahmeel was Hezron's firstborn son (1 Chron. 2:25). In rabbinic tradition, the Jerahmeel lineage is of interest because it represents an older line than the Ram line that led to David. Some scholars have attempted to link the Jerahmeelites to a distinct clan group in the Negev, mentioned in 1 Sam. 27:10 and 30:29.
